title: A Data science mode beside Developer: the same product drawn like Claude Code
request: The owner: keep DCLab's product UI as it is now as the Developer mode (the general UI), and add a Data science UI mode with the same functionality but very similar to Claude Code, more data-science friendly. The request was first misread: the new look was built in the separate dclab-code app (a Claude-style page at /next there) instead of DCLab's own product UI in this repository; the owner pointed at http://127.0.0.1:8765 and said it was a mistake.
spec: One switch in the top bar, Developer | Data science, kept in the browser. Developer is untouched. Data science changes only layout and look: the same views, scripts, API calls and controls. Home becomes a conversation (a greeting and one big box; then the chat as the main column with the reply box pinned at the bottom) and its context (what needs you, the workspace numbers, what DCLab understood, the team, Claude beside DCLab) sits in a right column, as Claude Code keeps its plan and context beside the session. Numbers in tables read as data (monospace, aligned). Light and dark. Fits 375 px.
plan: Read the product frontend: shell.html, core.js (router, roles, boot), the kit tokens, look.css and styles.css, and Home's markup and scripts.
Add the switch and a New chat row to the shell; setMode and placeRail in core.js.
Write ds.css: tokens on :root[data-mode=ds] (the page's aliases live on :root too), frame, flat cards, Home's conversation layout and right column; append it last in build.py.
Rebuild with make web; check in a throwaway server (no sign-in, no model, its own workspace) at 1440, 768 and 375 px, light and dark, both modes and the switch both ways.
Run the web build tests and the browser checks; add a browser check for the mode.
Independent review (dclab-reviewer, measured in real Chrome), fix its findings, extend the browser check, then commit.

decisions.why: styles.css defines its aliases (--bg, --panel, --accent...) on :root from the kit's --ts-* tokens; a custom property resolves where it is declared, so tokens changed on body would not reach them.

decisions.decision: Move Home's context cards into a right column with a small script instead of CSS only.
decisions.why: The cards are siblings at different depths of Home's overview pane; a CSS grid alone cannot stack them in a second column without sharing row heights with the conversation.

decisions.decision: Keep the solution workflow map in the conversation's column, not the right column.
decisions.why: It is a 950 by 352 drawing; at 340 px its labels are unreadable. In the 780 px column it reads at about 0.8 scale, like a plan card above the chat.

decisions.decision: Hide Home's start box while a chat is open in Data science; New chat brings it back.
decisions.why: Claude Code shows one box per session. The chat's own reply bar keeps Connect data and the step-by-step link; budget, who drives and the domain pack apply only when a draft starts.

decisions.decision: One switch, in the sidebar under the workspace, at every width; nothing added to the top bar.
decisions.why: The review measured that a switch in the top bar made Developer scroll sideways at 1150-1400 px (19 px at 1280, 65 px at 1200); a first fix only hid it at 760 px and below. The top bar is now the product's own, so Developer cannot change through it.

decisions.decision: Leave the existing role picker (Developer view, Business view...) as it is.
decisions.why: It changes who the product is shown to, not how it looks; the mode is a separate axis.

change: dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src/shell.html (switch in the top bar and the sidebar, New chat), core.js (setMode, placeRail, applied after the first page is shown), new ds.css (tokens, frame, Home's conversation layout, right column), build.py (ds.css last in app.css), static/app regenerated by make web, scripts/browser_e2e.py (check dsmode).

findings.defect: Switching from Data science back to Developer deleted Home's context cards (Needs you, the numbers, what DCLab understood, the team).
findings.scenario: Choose Data science, reload the page (the mode is kept), then press Developer: #home-inbox and the other cards are gone from the page.
findings.cause: placeRail kept references to the nodes it moved; started in Data science, it ran before Home's first show and the references no longer matched the live cards, so the stale copies were put back and the live rail was removed with the real cards inside.
findings.fix: placeRail is stateless: each time it looks up the live card by selector and the comment marking its place by its text; the rail is removed only when empty; the saved mode is applied after the first page is shown.
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check dsmode: starts in Data science, asserts each card exists exactly once, two round trips back to Developer with every card in its original parent.
findings.impact: Anyone who chose Data science and came back later lost Needs you, the workspace numbers, what DCLab understood and the team from Home after switching to Developer, until a reload.

findings.defect: The new switch made the page wider than the window, in Developer too.
findings.scenario: At 375 px the top bar measured 559 px (586 in Developer). After hiding it at 760 px and below, the review measured Developer still scrolling sideways at 1150-1400 px (19 px at 1280, 37 at 1366, 65 at 1200, 79 at 1150).
findings.cause: A 185-209 px switch in a top bar already filled by the search, the role picker and the theme button; below 1100 px the search turns into an icon, which is why phone and narrow checks passed.
findings.fix: The switch moved to the sidebar under the workspace, at every width; the top bar has nothing new.
findings.test: check dsmode measures Developer at 1150, 1280 and 1366 px and every page at 375 px in Data science; check mobile in Developer.
findings.impact: Every Developer user on a 1150-1400 px laptop got a page that scrolls sideways: the product as it was would have changed.
alternatives: Hide the top-bar switch at 760 px and below (the first fix): the review showed it still overflowed at laptop widths.
A compact top-bar switch: the role picker, the search and the theme button already fill the bar at 1150 px.

findings.defect: The sidebar's New chat button ran past the sidebar's right edge.
findings.scenario: At 1440 px the button was 225 px wide with a 12 px left margin in a 226 px column.
findings.cause: width: 100% on a menu row that already has a left margin.
findings.fix: width auto and no side margin.
findings.test: Checked in the browser (bounding box inside the sidebar).
findings.impact: A cut-off button at the top of the sidebar.

findings.defect: About 685 px of empty space below Home's conversation in Data science.
findings.scenario: Data science, 1280 px, an empty workspace: the overview pane 1145 px tall, its content ending at 460 px.
findings.cause: The right column spans 40 grid rows and the pane had an 18 px row gap, repeated between every pair of rows, empty ones too.
findings.fix: No row gap on the pane; the conversation column's parts are spaced by a top margin.
findings.test: check dsmode: at most 40 px between the last part and the pane's bottom during a chat.
findings.impact: Data science Home looked half empty and scrolled into blank space.

findings.defect: Data science lost a feature: with a chat open, the domain pack of the draft could not be changed.
findings.scenario: Data science, start a chat, look for the pack chooser: the whole start panel was hidden, and with it #home-pack-btn and #home-packs, which call choosePack on the open draft.
findings.cause: The rule hid the start panel whole, not only its box.
findings.fix: Only the start panel's parts other than the pack row and its cards are hidden while a chat is open.
findings.test: check dsmode: the pack row is visible during a chat.
findings.impact: A person in Data science could not change an open draft's domain pack, which Developer allows.

findings.defect: The browser check missed the risky paths: it never opened a chat, never measured Developer at desktop widths, never pressed New chat.
findings.scenario: F2's laptop-width overflow passed every check.
findings.cause: The check tested the switch on an empty Home only.
findings.fix: check dsmode now starts a chat in Data science (start box hidden, pack kept, context cards shown, no empty space, no sideways scroll), presses New chat (box back, cursor in it) and measures Developer at three laptop widths.

findings.defect: A visit that started in the kept Data science mode left no record of the mode (capture rule).
findings.scenario: Choose Data science, come back the next day: no click on the switch, so no event says the visit ran in it.
findings.fix: At start in the kept mode the page records a ui.action named mode-ds with target saved (an existing kind and its fields).
findings.test: none added: ui events already have their browser check (ui); the event kind and fields are unchanged.
findings.impact: The training records could not tell which look a session ran in when the switch was never clicked.

findings.defect: Two shadows (a toast's and a selected segment's) keep their light values in Data science dark.
findings.scenario: Data science, dark: a toast or the pressed half of a segmented control has a faint light-mode shadow.
findings.fix: Not taken: cosmetic, no effect on reading or use; left for a later look pass.

measurements.name: browser checks, all
measurements.result: 13 of 14 passed with the Mac's Chrome (DCLAB_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome; Playwright's Chromium was removed by a disk cleanup); poll failed once
limits: poll also failed 1 of 3 runs on the committed code without this change (the page's follow-up request timing), so it is not caused by this change; it is not fixed here

measurements.name: browser check dsmode
measurements.gate: 21 pages without an error and within 375 px in Data science; cards moved and returned twice
measurements.result: pass, with flow, mobile and pages, after the review's fixes: Developer within 1150, 1280 and 1366 px; a chat in Data science keeps the pack chooser and context, no empty space; New chat puts the cursor back
limits: checked on a throwaway server with no model and an empty workspace: no live conversation with a model was run in this mode

outcome: Data science mode is a switch away on every page; Developer is unchanged (13 of the existing 14 browser checks pass as before, and the one that does not is flaky without this change).
lessons: Before building a UI, open the exact page the person means; a similar request for another app of the owner was built in the wrong repository first.
A script that moves parts of a page must not keep references across the page's start: look them up live each time.
Adding a control to a crowded top bar needs a phone-width check in every mode, not only the new one.
risks: Only Home is laid out as a conversation; the other pages get the look (colours, flat cards, numbers) but keep their Developer layout.
The owner's own server on 8765 needs a reload of the page (and the build is served from static/app, so no restart) to show the switch.
